newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Commissions boosted Luxembourg banks' 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Commissions boosted Luxembourg banks' 1996 profits.

text.p: Luxembourg banks' 1996 gross profits rose 6.2 percent to 206 billion francs ($5.6 billion), boosted by stock trading and net commissions, the Luxembourg Monetary Institute (IML) said in its 1996 annual report.
The IML's latest quarterly bulletin, published at the same time, also showed banks' first-quarter 1997 gross profits rose 8.9 percent from a year ago.

For 1996, profits before provisions climbed 6.4 percent to 110.3 billion francs while results after provisions rose 15.4 percent to 105.8 billion. Net profits jumped 17.4 percent to 71.571 billion francs.

"The important increase in 1996 net profits...is the result of two influences," the annual report said. "The first consists in factors increasing the level of profits on banks' credit and other financial activities, and the second, whose impact dominates, rests in the actual utilisation of the resources initially produced."
The report noted in 1996, interest rate margins rose a modest 0.3 percent, reducing their share in gross results to a historical low 61.8 percent.
This was partly because during 1996, all relevant interest rates fell, resulting in a reduction of gross interest flows earned and paid out.
Competition also increased, hurting interest rate margins.
Other gross results components displayed "a much more dynamic evolution," the report said.
The report specifically noted net profits on securities trading, which jumped 28.8 percent, and net commissions, which grew 26 percent to a record level of more than 54 billion francs.
Stock trading picked up as market expectations in 1996 of continued vigorous economic growth and low inflation pushed long-term interest rates down and favoured stock prices.
Banks had seized the opportunity and taken profits on their securities portfolios, while the good performance of stock prices had knock-on effects on net commissions earnings.
Despite new hirings during the year, labour cost increases were limited to 4.3 percent due to productivity gains, a new sector wage agreement and the absence of a wage indexation round.
At 4.5 billion francs, net provisions absorbed a record low 2.2 percent of gross results.
The weighted average solvency ratio, which takes into account each credit institution's volume of activity, had shown continous improvement and stood at 12.5 percent at end-1996.
The aggregate balance sheet of all the banks established in Luxembourg rose 4.8 percent to 19.257 billion francs by end 1996 compared to end 1995.
The number of banks registered in Luxembourg increased by one in 1996, bringing the total to 221.
